physics_notes:
# wire_caddy — realism QA repair

Open black wire basket, tall bent legs and small rubber feet; no filled wall proxies.

## Evidence and numerical review

Three original calibrated frames: f0168, f0008, f0194. Mean silhouette IoU 0.1127. Photo contours are hand traced, with approximately 2–4 px uncertainty at 256 px crop resolution. Explicit masks exclude selected occluders. Wire masks additionally use a dark-pixel threshold. This is not certified segmentation ground truth.

Comparison: [photo / render / overlay](../review/wire_caddy_compare.jpg). Full calibration, masks and measurements: `../review/wire_caddy/`.

Grades: evidence=B, silhouette=F, proportions=C, colour_texture=C, articulation=A, physics=C, collision=B, instances=B

## Changes

- Added three original calibrated photo crops, traced photo masks and numerical comparisons.
- Added explicit mass basis/uncertainty, constituent density, material-specific friction, restitution, COM prior and fragility.
- Replaced solid collision panels with individual wire segment colliders.
- Reduced wire counts and raised basket floor to match taller visible legs.
- Added small rubber foot caps; preserved open gaps and graspable wire structure.

## Remaining

- Thin-wire photo segmentation and reconstructed camera pose are sensitive to 1–3 pixel errors.
- Silhouette IoU remains poor and does not meet requested A/B standard.
- Wire bends, spacing and occlusion still need higher-quality matching.
- Real present mass, friction, restitution and stiffness have not been measured; physics values are explicit priors.

Run `~/blender/blender -b --python-exit-code 1 -P build.py` from this asset directory. Run `qa_render.py -- wire_caddy` through Blender from the set directory for calibrated QA renders. Blender/OBJ use metres, +Z up; GLB uses +Y up. Physics is disabled on Blender load for review; external scene support surfaces are required. Deformable metadata requires simulator integration; current Blender dynamics use rigid compound fallbacks.


## Round 2

Grades before: {"evidence": "B", "silhouette": "F", "proportions": "C", "colour_texture": "C", "articulation": "A", "physics": "C", "collision": "B", "instances": "B"}

Grades after: {"evidence": "B", "silhouette": "F", "proportions": "B", "colour_texture": "B", "articulation": "A", "physics": "B", "collision": "B", "instances": "B"}

Mean IoU 0.1127 -> 0.1531; same-mask RGB distance 0.3708.

- Preserved colour transforms, glass IOR/optical thickness/absorption and metal anisotropy in portable GLB material extensions; procedural bump/SSS remain renderer-dependent.
- Re-measured source depth with ktools in all three review frames; retained depth/calibration uncertainty.
- Replaced unexplained mass priors with explicit constituent volume × density or textile-area budgets; synchronized part masses and COM metadata.
- Added portable MJCF rigid contacts and checked all convex collision meshes.
- Re-fitted rail and foot landmarks across three calibrated frames; RMS 41.03 px to 9.85 px at 512 px crop resolution.
- Replaced the tubular top frame with the photographed flat band.
- Corrected U-shaped leg connections to span the short ends; added the raised lower bends and individual wire contacts.
- Updated wire counts and dimensions; kept open basket and wire-grasp clearances.

Remaining:

- Raw wire IoU remains very low: dark-pixel photo masks also include shadows/occluding textile, and subpixel wire alignment is sensitive to calibration. The low score is retained.
- Wire spacing, bends and camera residuals still prevent strict silhouette sign-off.
- Mass, friction, restitution and stiffness remain estimates, not measured physical calibration.
- Mean silhouette IoU remains below the unchanged 0.80 threshold; no automatic promotion to B.

See model.json physics.mass_budget, simulation/rigid.xml, and (for soft assets) simulation/deformable.xml. Generated microtextures are inferred detail, never source evidence.

physics_properties.mass_basis: Sum of explicit constituent mass_budget components; see dimensions, density and assumptions there.
physics_properties.mass_status: material-density / geometry estimate; not a weighed or verified real-product mass
physics_properties.density_basis: constituent solid prior, NOT envelope density
physics_properties.friction_basis: user-specified material range; sponge and textile are tentative
physics_properties.center_of_mass_basis: Mass-weighted volume centroids of material-budget components; estimated fill/ballast/textile densities.

mass_budget.basis: Sum of thin convex contact-piece volumes × constituent density; small piece overlaps can bias mass upward.

physics_properties.contact_geometry: collision/ convex parts, independently mapped to part IDs in model.json

density_sources.title: Outokumpu Core stainless data
density_sources.use: Stainless solid density approx 7900 kg/m³; grade is not identified.

density_sources.title: Smooth-On foam density data
density_sources.use: Reference for distinction between foam bulk and constituent density; this sponge grade is not identified.

physics_properties.estimated_dry_or_filled: Filled state for soap/syrup/pump/bread/food/tea; dry state for textiles/sponge/scourer.
physics_properties.blender_inertia_limit: Blender fallback mass is synchronized; its pivot/inertia is approximate. MJCF specifies explicit material-budget COM and estimated inertias.

limitations: Individual convex octagonal wire segments preserve basket gaps and grasp clearance.

provenance.geometry: Reconstructed from kitchen video; hidden surfaces are completed. Scale and material appearance remain approximate.
provenance.motion: Observed trajectories where documented; unobserved axes and endpoints are assumptions.
provenance.forces: Simulation measurements of assumed parameters; not force measurements from video.
